name: Spot-confirmed favourite, wide price range
description: Once per 15-minute market on BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE, buys the favourite (YES or NO) at 120-480 s before close when spot is at least 2.5 sigma (15-min realized vol, basis-corrected) past the strike and the ask is at most 98.5c; held to settlement. btc-zfav's rule with a higher z, a higher price cap and more checkpoints, so it trades many more markets.
hypothesis: Late favourites are priced as if less settled than they are: Kalshi quoters under-weight how far spot is from the strike in vol units, and the gap is worth more than the taker fee even at 95-98c where the fee is tiny. Other side: sellers of near-certain contracts and flat-vol quoters. Dev screen (research dataset, Dec-Aug, taker next fills net of fee, one entry per market at the earliest qualifying checkpoint, z>=2.5, ask<=98.5c): 9,563 entries (35/day), +1.34c (se 0.13), 9/9 months, every coin positive (BTC 1.26, ETH 1.12, SOL 2.27, XRP 1.84, DOGE 1.82). Parameters fixed from this screen before any pipeline run. Wrong if the engine's depth/latency/fees erase it, <60% months positive, 2x latency negative, or it decays like sol-zfav in the lockbox. Rare losses cost ~98c each (about 1.7% of entries), so it is a thin-edge/fat-left-tail shape.
